description: The House this week passed significant legislation to protect Georgia ratepayers and announced the launch of legislation that will further help with the affordability of the insurance market. Protecting Georgia’s Ratepayers HB 1063, passed the House! This legislation protects residential and retail electricity customers from costs associated with data center construction and operation. HB 1063 safeguards energy affordability for Georgia families and small businesses by ensuring that data centers and large-load consumers pay their own way upfront. Checkout the Speaker’s statement here: https://loom.ly/vyfNUuo The House Blue-Ribbon Study Committee on Insurance Rates met over the summer and worked alongside Insurance Commissioner John King and policy experts from Georgia State University and the University of Georgia to draft the following legislation. With this legislation, Georgia’s insurance market will further stabilize and provide relief to ratepayers. HB 1344, The Insurance Affordability & Claims Integrity Act Increase nearly 40 insurance fines in Georgia’s insurance code. Strengthens enforcement of uninsured motorist laws Cracks down on insurance fraud. Implements the Fortified Homes Program to shore up homes against storm damage. HB 1274, Excess Auto Insurance Profits Act If a company profits 5% above expected profit for 3 straight years, it must file a rate decrease. Florida and several other states do this, and in one case, it reduced rates by $1 billion for a single company. HB 1262, Fine Increase Bill Surprise Billing, Mental Health, and General Fine authority is increased from $2,000 to $10,000 and from $10,000 to $25,000. HB 1263, The Premium Tax Clawback Act Currently, insurance companies can pursue refunds for premium tax payment “errors” over long periods of time. This bill shortens the clawback period to 3 years. Read Speaker Burn's statement on insurance affordability here: https://loom.ly/TlKGI_c Here are some other bills that have passed the House this week: HB 541 expands the tuition equalization grant eligibility to include higher education institutions that offer baccalaureate programs in nursing, have maintained a physical presence in Georgia for 10 years, and hold accreditation from either the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education as well as accreditation from either the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools or a regional accrediting agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. HB 662 amends the definition of “rural hospital organization” to include “rural freestanding emergency department.” With this definition change, more rural hospitals will be eligible to receive tax credits. Preston Fant and Brant Chesney Firefighter Safety Act, HB 1086, will require the owner of any commercial or industrial building that was constructed using light-frame truss-type construction to post a notice. This will protect firefighters since this type of construction burns more quickly, which can cause sudden roof and floor collapse. HB 970 will expand the list of qualified healthcare professionals who can conduct sports physicals for student athletes. These physicals will also include a cardiovascular prescreening to take proactive steps to identify health risks for student athletes.
title: Week 6 Recap, Protecting Ratepayers and Children-Rep.Carmen Rice
